page: Microsoft Azure F4als_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Falsv6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The server features 4 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 4 vCPUs. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-CPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. There is no bundled local storage, though the instance is premium storage capable, and it contains no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the top tier (top 10%) and Geekbench single-core scores in the top 25%. The hardware supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration such as AES and SHA_NI. However, memory performance is a notable bottleneck; uncached large-block read memory bandwidth and the PassMark memory score both fall into the bottom 25%. Multi-core performance for both stress-ng and Geekbench remains in the average range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F4als_v6 offers high single-thread compute capabilities relative to its resource footprint, making it a viable option for CPU-bound tasks that do not require large memory allocations. Due to the 8.0 GB memory limitation and weak uncached memory bandwidth, it is less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale LLM inference. It is best suited for web serving, lightweight software compilation, single-threaded batch processing, and general-purpose compute workloads with low memory footprints.
